output.content:
**AI accelerator market share depends materially on the denominator**—GPU-only versus all AI chips, and revenue versus server shipments. [[1]]

| 2024 global AI-server market measure | NVIDIA | AMD | Custom silicon / ASICs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **GPU-equipped AI servers: chip-supplier share** | **Nearly 90%** | **~8%** | Not applicable to the GPU-only denominator |
| **All AI-server chips (GPU, ASIC, FPGA): chip-supplier share** | **~64%** | Not separately disclosed in this measure | The balance is largely ASICs, FPGAs and other suppliers |
| **AI-server mix by system type** | GPUs: **~71%** of AI servers | Included in GPU category | ASIC servers: **~26%** |

TrendForce’s 2024 estimate puts NVIDIA at nearly 90% of the GPU-equipped AI-server market and AMD at roughly 8%; once proprietary ASICs and FPGAs are included, NVIDIA’s share falls to about 64%. [[1]] GPU-based servers represented about 71% of AI servers in 2024, versus approximately 26% for ASIC-based servers, reflecting sizeable deployment of proprietary accelerators by AWS, Meta and other North American cloud providers, as well as Chinese developers. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** NVIDIA retains overwhelming leadership in merchant AI GPUs, while AMD is the principal merchant GPU challenger but remains much smaller. [[1]] Custom silicon—such as Google TPUs and cloud-provider in-house ASICs—is the principal source of NVIDIA share dilution when the market is defined to include all accelerators rather than GPUs alone. [[2]] [[1]]

**Direction of travel:** TrendForce estimated NVIDIA would still hold approximately 70% of the broader AI-chip market in 2025, but expected greater custom-ASIC deployment to reduce that share over time. [[3]] Its 2026 shipment forecast has GPUs still leading at 69.7% of AI-server shipments, while ASIC-based systems rise to 27.8%, their highest share since 2023, with ASIC shipment growth outpacing GPU-system growth. [[4]] 

These figures should not be treated as interchangeable with revenue share: NVIDIA’s premium systems mean that its revenue share can exceed its shipment or unit share. [[5]]
